The file is already accessible at www.bibiugames.com/app-ads.txt and returns a 200 response from GitHub.

The apex domain bibiugames.com/app-ads.txt returns a 404. Its DNS A records point to AWS CloudFront rather than GitHub Pages.

The apex domain likely points to a different host than www. AdMob crawlers check the root domain directly and may not follow redirects to www. The IAB app-ads.txt specification governs how crawlers handle this.

The IAB specification allows crawlers to follow HTTP redirects to a maximum of five or ten hops, provided the final URL remains on the same root domain or a subdomain. Google's documentation explicitly requires the app-ads.txt file to be published at the root of the developer website.

Google documentation states that if the developer website redirects, the app-ads.txt file must be placed on the final destination. If bibiugames.com redirects to www.bibiugames.com, the file belongs on the www domain. If the apex domain returns a 404 without redirecting, Google will not locate the file during crawls.

A PowerShell probe of the apex domain failed with an invalid operation error. This usually signals a redirect mishandled by the tool. I will use curl to inspect the HTTP headers for redirects on both the apex and www domains.
